minutes.headline: Capital Planning set four presentation dates for FY25 requests and reviewed scoring; no formal votes beyond adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed the Colin scoring criteria and the list of capital requests received for this year, then debated how to weigh buildings like Town Hall, TC Passo and Brooks House given the Municipal Building Committee's plans. It settled on four meeting dates for department presentations, with schools pushed late so the new facilities director can be included. The meeting adjourned by voice vote.

budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the total of the requests received as the summary of projects to be reviewed.
A member asked for last year's final figure; it was recalled roughly and said to be affected by the tax situation.

budget_items.topic: Fire trucks and special purpose stabilization
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the forecast fire truck purchases over four fiscal years and that the special purpose stabilization account holds a similar sum, with an article to spend part of it.
A member recalled the town manager's fiscal forecast showing a substantial deficit in projected capital spending.
Members said the cost of the renovation and annex is unknown but likely very large, with ARPA money granted for engineering.
Cemetery projects would likely exceed the cemetery's receipts reserved account, which is not a revolving account voted at town meeting.

decisions.decision: Presentation meetings chosen for November 6, 8, 20 (7 p.m. start) and 29, all in the Ritter building lower conference room; others at 6 p.m.
Schools to present on the 20th or 29th; DPW, facilities and schools each get their own night, and fire/police can be combined.
Departments to be asked to supply presentations in PowerPoint rather than PDF, ahead of the meeting.
Chair to email the four dates and try to book meetings several weeks ahead; meetings will be recorded.
Departments that combined planning and construction in one project number may be asked to split or explain it in their presentation.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee chose four dates for FY25 capital request presentations: November 6, 8, 20 and 29.
Schools are to present on the 20th or 29th, so the new facilities director can be included; DPW, facilities and schools each get their own night.
Members debated how to weigh Town Hall, TC Passo and Brooks House given the Municipal Building Committee's plans, and reached no resolution.
The committee reviewed the scoring criteria and their weaknesses and kept the question open; no votes were taken beyond adjournment.
Departments will be asked for PowerPoint presentations, and those that combined planning and construction under one project number may be asked to split or explain it.

why_it_matters: Capital requests such as buildings, fire trucks and school facilities are ranked in this process before they reach a Town Meeting vote, and the scoring method for building projects is still unsettled.

The cost of the municipal building renovation was described as unknown but likely large, and members recalled a forecast deficit in projected capital spending, so competing requests may face tight limits.
